facts.raw_span: one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
a single episode of urinary incontinence
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy

concepts.why: The patient's left leg pain and weakness, along with the MRI findings of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy, support the diagnosis of iliopsoas tendinitis.
The patient's history of gout, along with the presence of joint effusion and elevated inflammatory markers, suggests the possibility of crystal arthropathy.

The patient's symptoms of left leg pain and weakness, along with the presence of urinary incontinence, raise the possibility of cauda equina syndrome, although the MRI findings do not support this diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms of left leg pain and weakness, along with the presence of elevated inflammatory markers and pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury, raise the possibility of epidural abscess, although the MRI findings do not support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of left leg pain and weakness, along with the MRI findings of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement, support the diagnosis of muscle strain.
The patient's history of chronic kidney disease, along with the presence of pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury, supports the diagnosis of chronic kidney disease.
The patient's history of hypertension, along with the presence of elevated blood pressure, supports the diagnosis of hypertension.
The patient's history of hyperlipidaemia, along with the presence of elevated inflammatory markers, supports the diagnosis of hyperlipidaemia.

rationales.F01: Left leg pain and weakness is consistent with iliopsoas tendinitis.
rationales.F03: Urinary incontinence could be a sign of cauda equina syndrome.
rationales.F05: Low blood pressure is not typical of hypertension.
rationales.F09: Elevated inflammatory markers could indicate infection or inflammation, such as epidural abscess or crystal arthropathy.
rationales.F10: Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury is consistent with chronic kidney disease.
rationales.F11: Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement is highly suggestive of iliopsoas tendinitis.
